answer: Insider run many fake agents like seeds in one orchard. Identity mechanism tie reputation to proof-of-work pulse, so each agent must burn compute capital to birth. That expense creates cost barrier: fake agents drain real resources, no free proliferation. Reputation bridge then let honest agents verify each other's origin pulse, blocking duplicates from joining consensus or claiming rewards. Constraint: privileged insider still pay full compute price per fake agent, making large sybil swarm economically irrational.
